Metadata.title: Yahya Chanat — Full-Stack Software Engineer
Metadata.description: Full-Stack Software Engineer building web products across frontend, backend APIs, databases, real-time systems, background jobs, AI integrations, and deployment.

Hero.intro: I’m a Full-Stack Software Engineer building production-oriented web applications and SaaS products. I work across responsive frontend, backend APIs, databases, real-time features, background jobs, AI integrations, and deployment.

Work.label: Case studies
Work.intro: These projects cover more than their interfaces: frontend flows, APIs, authentication, data models, payments, real-time messaging, background execution, AI features, and deployment decisions.

About.label: The engineer behind the work
About.portraitHelp: Add a photo of yourself — set about.portrait in lib/site.ts.
About.heading: I engineer the complete product, including the systems behind the interface.
About.p1: I’m Yahya Chanat, a Full-Stack Software Engineer and Software Engineering student at Fırat University, with graduation expected in 2028. I build production-oriented web applications, SaaS platforms, and e-commerce systems from product flow through deployment.
About.p2: On the frontend I use React, Next.js, and TypeScript. On the backend I build Node.js services and REST APIs with NestJS or Express, model data in PostgreSQL and MongoDB, and implement authentication, payment, and webhook flows.
About.p3: My projects also include Socket.io messaging, BullMQ jobs backed by Redis, AI-assisted content tools, social-platform integrations, multilingual interfaces with Arabic RTL, and deployment work with Docker and Nginx.
About.e1: Frontend flows that connect cleanly to APIs
About.e2: Backend services, authentication, and data models
About.e3: Real-time features and reliable background jobs
About.e4: AI integrations, deployment, and product delivery

Process.label: How I work
Process.intro: I connect product decisions to the frontend, backend, data, integrations, and deployment needed to make the workflow complete.
Process.s1Body: Clarify the user flow, requirements, boundaries, and failure cases before choosing an implementation.
Process.s2Body: Map the interface states, API contracts, and data relationships so the frontend and backend share a clear structure.
Process.s3Body: Implement the responsive UI, services, database access, and authentication as one connected product flow.
Process.s4Body: Add payments, webhooks, background jobs, real-time communication, or AI only where the product needs them, then verify success and error paths.
Process.s5Body: Prepare the application for deployment, validate the production build and responsive behavior, and keep the system maintainable after launch.

Skills.label: Engineering toolkit
Skills.intro: A stack grounded in shipped portfolio work: user interfaces, APIs, databases, asynchronous processing, external services, and deployment.
Skills.strength1Body: I take a feature from requirements and interface states through backend behavior, integration, and deployment.
Skills.strength2Body: I build REST APIs, authentication and webhook flows, then connect them to PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and background workers.
Skills.strength3Body: I have implemented real-time messaging, payment workflows, social APIs, file uploads, and AI-assisted product features.
Skills.frontendNote: Responsive, localized interfaces built with typed React and Next.js.
Skills.backendNote: Node.js services, REST endpoints, authentication, webhooks, and WebSockets.
Skills.dataNote: Relational and document data with queues, caching, delayed work, and retries.
Skills.deliveryNote: Containers, reverse proxying, source control, payments, media, and AI services.

Journey.label: Experience & education
Journey.intro: Backend AI engineering experience, independent full-stack product work, and a Software Engineering degree.
Journey.flyBody: Currently interning at FlyRank AI, focusing on Backend AI Engineering.
Journey.degreeBody: Pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Software Engineering, with graduation expected in 2028.
Journey.independentBody: Building YSHAI, YASHSTORE, YASHBLOG, YASHCHAT, and other applications across frontend, backend APIs, databases, integrations, and deployment.

Contact.intro: I’m open to full-stack opportunities, internships, and product collaborations. Email is the best way to reach me.

yshai.tagline: AI-powered social media management, end to end
yshai.problem: Creators, brands, and teams need to plan content, manage connected social accounts, publish on schedule, and review performance without splitting the workflow across separate tools.
yshai.contribution: Built the product independently from end to end: a Next.js and React interface, a NestJS and PostgreSQL backend, and workflows for connected accounts, content drafts, scheduling, campaigns, media, analytics, and AI-assisted content creation.
yshai.decision1: Kept durable publishing state in PostgreSQL while BullMQ and Redis handle delayed execution and retries in background workers.
yshai.decision2: Used a protected Next.js proxy for authenticated browser requests to the NestJS API, keeping the frontend and backend as separate applications.
yshai.decision3: Structured the interface around English, Arabic, and Turkish locale routes, including right-to-left handling for Arabic.
yshai.outcome: Shipped the product as a private beta and learned how to design a larger backend around background jobs, queues, and caching strategies, then deploy and operate it on a VPS.

yashblog.tagline: A full-stack platform for writing and publishing
yashblog.problem: Building a blogging platform means connecting an approachable writing flow with accounts, post management, discovery, and reader interactions in one coherent application.
yashblog.contribution: Built the frontend and backend independently, including authentication and profiles, Tiptap-based authoring, post creation and editing, publish state, categories, likes, comments, and post search and filtering.
yashblog.decision1: Separated the Next.js frontend from an Express REST API, with MongoDB models accessed through Mongoose.
yashblog.decision2: Used Tiptap for rich-text authoring and added a staged write, details, and preview flow before publication.
yashblog.decision3: Modeled publication state, categories, likes, and threaded comment relationships directly in the post and comment schemas.
yashblog.outcome: Completed a responsive full-stack blogging application that covers the core path from creating an account and writing a post to publishing and discussing it.

yashchat.problem: I wanted to understand how a real-time application moves messages between clients while retaining accounts, conversations, and message history.
yashchat.contribution: Built the application independently, covering registration and login, one-to-one conversation creation, the responsive chat interface, Socket.io messaging, MongoDB persistence, and light and dark themes.
yashchat.decision1: Scoped Socket.io traffic to conversation rooms so messages are sent to the relevant one-to-one chat.
yashchat.decision2: Authenticated socket connections with JWT before allowing a client to join a room or send a message.
yashchat.decision3: Persisted messages through Mongoose and loaded recent conversation history when a client joins a chat.
yashchat.outcome: Completed the application and developed a practical understanding of real-time communication with WebSockets and Socket.io.

yashstore.tagline: A complete storefront and Stripe checkout flow
yashstore.problem: I built YASHSTORE to learn how a full e-commerce journey connects product discovery, cart state, payment, order creation, and store administration.
yashstore.contribution: Built the project independently, including the product catalog, cart and checkout, NextAuth configuration for credentials and Google providers, customer orders, and an admin dashboard for products, categories, users, and order status.
yashstore.decision1: Modeled users, products, categories, carts, and orders in PostgreSQL through Prisma.
yashstore.decision2: Connected Stripe Payment Element to a server-created PaymentIntent, then verified webhook signatures before creating an order and clearing its cart items.
yashstore.decision3: Separated customer shopping views from a role-aware admin area for catalog and order management.
yashstore.outcome: Completed the end-to-end store flow and learned how to integrate Stripe payments with application-side cart and order data.

yashtask.tagline: Full-stack task management with AI-assisted planning
yashtask.problem: I built YASHTASK to learn how authenticated users can organize projects, track task progress, and explore AI-generated planning suggestions in one full-stack application.
yashtask.contribution: Built the project independently, including authentication, project creation and editing, task creation and deletion, status tracking, and a guided planning flow backed by Google Gemini.
yashtask.decision1: Used Next.js server actions with Mongoose models to keep each authenticated user's projects and tasks in MongoDB.
yashtask.decision2: Represented task progress with Pending, In Progress, and Completed states and grouped project tasks around those states.
yashtask.decision3: Used the Vercel AI SDK with a Zod schema to request structured weekly suggestions from Gemini; generated plans are not persisted as projects or tasks.
yashtask.outcome: Built a working project and task workflow while learning full-stack data handling, authentication, status-based interfaces, and structured AI output.

quizyourself.problem: I built QuizYourself as a university project to help students turn material from their lecture slides into reusable self-testing quizzes.
quizyourself.contribution: Built the application independently with authenticated quiz creation, manual entry of questions and answer choices, a shared quiz browser, immediate scoring feedback, and creator profiles for managing saved quizzes.
quizyourself.decision1: Stored each quiz as a MongoDB document containing its slug, questions, choices, and correct-answer indexes.
quizyourself.decision2: Kept quiz authoring explicit and manual: creators enter each question, its answer choices, and the correct answer.
quizyourself.decision3: Calculated results in the quiz interface so students can see their total score and per-question correctness after submission.
quizyourself.outcome: Completed the university project and received an A+ for the implemented quiz creation and self-assessment workflow.
